The second review of 1.24.37's AI_ELECTRONICS mends (36965b4), against afea882 and 22b1c03
==========================================================================================

Written by a reviewer who had not seen the mends drafted and did not read the first review's cases, fixtures,
test or findings (tests/fixtures/review_electronics_1237/, review_notes_ans_1237/, tests/electronics_load_1237.js,
tests/review_*_1237.py). Every case is my own: questions as people ask them, replies as models write them, and the
bench's own electronics replies from tests/fixtures/bench_run_*.json (bench-* cases).

What was run
------------
- 210 cases (cases.js), each built with L.aiAct.build(reply, question) in jsdom (lib.js, through
  tests/fixtures/liftstation_review1_1230/load.js) on all three versions, side by side:
      22b1c03: 152 AGREE, 58 DISAGREE        afea882: 179 AGREE, 31 DISAGREE        36965b4: 165 AGREE, 45 DISAGREE
  133 are right replies that drew on 22b1c03 and must draw the same ("keep": same branches, pins, transistors,
  resistors, diodes and no new note); 5 bench replies must come out as they did ("same"); 42 must draw a stated
  circuit; 30 must be questioned with a stated line.
- run_36965b4.txt is replay.js on 36965b4. The working tree moved to 2634e18 during the review (a change outside
  AI_ELECTRONICS, line 45897); replay.js on it prints the same, line for line.
- Every bench prompt is unchanged: prompts.js built the full prompt, the short prompt and the MAKE action's prompt for
  all 300 bench questions (sets A and B) on the three versions -- 900 prompts each, all the same.
- Not run: npm test, any browser, any model. Drawings were judged by their structure (branches, parts, what drives
  what), not by eye.

Three-way table (22b1c03 / afea882 / 36965b4; A agree, D disagree)
  AAA 132   all right throughout
  DAA  20   mended by afea882, kept by 36965b4
  DDA  13   mended by 36965b4 (a bare transistor line, the board's name for a pin, an LED's transistor, a button's transistor)
  AAD  17   NEW BREAKS in 36965b4: 11 right replies refused (H1), 3 spare pins (H3), 3 input lines (H4)
  ADD   3   broken by afea882 and not mended (t-fan-35b high; ask-button-spare medium; add-second-same-pin low)
  DAD  10   afea882 right, 36965b4 wrong again (medium)
  DDD  15   old faults, wrong in all three (13), plus mend-p02 (newly DRAWN wrong) and pin-01-said (new, low)

Counts of what 36965b4 broke or still gets wrong
  high    19 cases, 4 causes   (H1 12, H2 1, H3 3, H4 3)
  medium  11 cases, 5 causes   (the reply's own line handed back: also in 2 old-fault cases below)
  low      2 cases (new code)
  old     13 cases wrong in all three versions (1 of them a wrong drawing)

HIGH
----
H1. A right reply that drew on 22b1c03 is now refused: "Lantern could not draw this circuit correctly (Q1 does not
    switch M2's lower end to 0 V)". 12 cases: t-fan-alwayson, t-led-power, t-led-power2, t-lamp-pilot, t-relay-manual,
    t-pump-float, t-valve-two, t-led-direct, t-fan-two-q, t-buzzer-sw, t-led-button (all AAD) and t-fan-35b (ADD: the
    35B's own "transistor Q1 K1 P1 / motor M1 Q1", which afea882 already broke).
    The shape: the load's own line names its transistor ("motor M1 Q1", the 35B's way on the bench: bench_run_1256_35b_setb.json), the
    transistor's line names no load ("transistor Q1 P1", or the guide's K1), and the block has another load of the
    asked kind left on purpose -- a power LED always on beside a status LED, a fan that always runs, a pilot lamp, a
    second relay or a pump on its own switch, an LED lit straight from the same pin. The retarget (line 38122) takes
    that load as "the one <kind> for it to switch" and puts it under Q1 too: two loads on one transistor, and verify
    refuses the drawing. namesLoad (line 38115) looks only at the transistor's own line, never at a load's line that
    names the transistor; so Q1 already switches M1 and is given M2 as well.
    The question words the user gave ("always runs", "always on", "worked by a toggle switch") are what the drawing on
    22b1c03 showed. Tried in a scratch copy only (not in the repo): one line after line 38115,
        if (items.some(function (x) { return LOAD.test(x.role) && x.refs.indexOf(t.id) >= 0; })) return;
    turns all 12 back to AGREE and changes no other case of the 210. It needs trying by someone else before it goes in.
    Even with it, "on the transistor's own pin or on none" (line 38123) lets a load on its own switch through
    ("motor M1 S1"), and a load lit straight from the transistor's own pin (t-led-direct): both are driven already.

H2. A reply 22b1c03 and afea882 questioned is now DRAWN wrong, with one push button drawn twice. mend-p02:
        lamp L1 "12 V" / switch S1 L1 / transistor Q1 S1      (QP1: "a push button switches a 12 V lamp through an NPN")
    The retarget makes Q1 switch L1 (it says "Q1's line names no part to switch: L1 is the one lamp ..."); S1's line
    names L1, so S1 is both in the lamp's line (b.sw, line 38145) and on Q1's base (b.qsw, line 38149): the parts are
    "L1 Q1 R1 S1 S1". The double drawing itself is old -- old-sw-double ("switch S1 L1 / transistor Q1 L1 S1") draws
    S1 twice on all three versions -- but 36965b4 now leads a second, likelier way of writing it into that drawing.

H3. A spare pin is called spare when the question asks for two of the kind. ask-two-leds, ask-two-relays,
    ask-two-motors (AAD):
        QD5 "two LEDs, one on pin 12 and one on pin 13": pin P1 "D12" / pin P2 "D13" / led D1 P1 red
        -> "pin P2 drives or reads nothing: the led is driven already -- leave P2's line out, or name it on a part's
           line (led D1 P2, switch S1 P2)"
    Done as told, one LED (one relay, one motor) is drawn for a question that asks for two; the other line offered,
    "led D1 P2", names the first LED again (old, ask-two-leds-dup). pinLine's spare (line 38261) counts only that every
    load of the kind is driven, not how many the question asks for. The line for P2 is the second one's:
    "led D2 P2" / "relay K2 ..." with "transistor Q2 K2 P2" (no version gives it: ask-two-relays-line).
    ask-button-spare (ADD, medium) is the same message where the question asks for a push button: "leave P2's line
    out" drops the button asked for; 22b1c03 offered only lines.

H4. A pin whose label says input, read or sensor gets one line back, "switch S1 <pin>", whatever the question asks
    to read. ask-ldr-input (QD4, an LDR on A0), ask-pot-input (a pot on A0), ask-therm-read (QP3, a thermistor):
        pin P1 "A0 input" / pin P2 "D9" / led D1 P2  -> "pin P1 drives or reads nothing: name it on a part's line (switch S1 P1)"
    Copied, it draws a push button where the LDR, pot or thermistor goes, and the drawing passes. 22b1c03 listed
    "switch S1 P1" among three lines (none right either: ask-ldr-line, old); 36965b4 makes it the only one (line
    38259). The line is the one the question asks for: sensor LDR1 P1, pot RV1 P1, thermistor TH1 P1. (Also: S1 is
    used whether or not a switch S1 is already on another pin -- ask-switch-dup, old; and \bread matches "ready".)

MEDIUM (a plain miss afea882 got right)
------
M1. "led" added to the kinds a question asks for (line 38098) makes every question that also names an LED ask two
    kinds, so nothing is mended: two-relay-led (QX1 "a relay ... with an LED that shows when the relay is on",
    "transistor Q1 K1 P1" with the relay's own line left out, the LED on P2), two-motor-led (QX4), two-led-lamp and
    two-led-lamp2 (QX5 "a 12 V LED lamp": one lamp). All DAD. The line handed back is then 22b1c03's
    "transistor Q1 D1 P1": copied, it puts the indicator LED under the relay's transistor (old).
M2. The stepper/servo/AC exclusion empties every kind when the question names a stepper or servo anywhere:
    stepper-fan (QS1 "a 12 V cooling fan for my stepper motor driver") and servo-relay (QS3 "a 5 V relay ... to cut
    the power to my servos"). The fan and the relay are the loads asked for; afea882 drew both. Excluding the motor
    kind only where the motor asked for is the stepper or servo would keep them. (ac-motor-m, a 230 V AC motor under
    a 12 V NPN, is rightly questioned on all three.)
M3. The added part is refused beside any load that is not an LED with no pin: own-line-led (QR1; "led D1 P2 green"
    on its own pin, "transistor Q1 K1 P1", the relay's line left out). The LED on its own pin is not "drawn always on";
    afea882 drew it right. Questioned instead with "like: transistor Q1 K1 P1" and "(transistor Q1 K1 P1)" -- the
    reply's own line, twice (own-line-led-msg): copied, nothing changes (rule 3). The line to write is
    relay K1 "12 V coil". The same own line comes back in ask-own-line-buzzer and ask-own-line-ledk (listed under old:
    22b1c03 handed back another wrong line there).
M4. The board's-name rule reads a load's id at the end of a pin's label as that pin: pin-06 (pin P1 "D7 to K1" /
    transistor Q1 K1 P1, the relay's line left out) and pin-07 (pin P1 "Arduino D7 for relay K1"). K1 becomes P1, so
    the relay afea882 added is gone, and the reply is told "transistor Q1 K1 P1" -- its own line. A label that ends in
    the id of a load kind (K, M, L, Y, BZ, an LED's D) should not be read as a pin's name, nor a ref when the line
    names that pin already.
M5. ask-button-spare: see H3.

LOW
---
L1. pin-01-said: reading "D7" on the transistor's line as P2 changes what the model wrote and is not said (rule 2);
    the drawing is right. Same for pin-02..05 and pin-09.
L2. add-second-same-pin (ADD, from afea882): one relay asked; "transistor Q2 K2 P1" beside "transistor Q1 K1 P1"
    and relay K1 -> K2 is added, and two transistors are drawn on P1. The code's note says the review meant to stop
    "two transistors on one pin"; this path still does it.

Old faults (wrong on 22b1c03, afea882 and 36965b4)
----------
- old-sw-double (a wrong drawing): "switch S1 L1 / transistor Q1 L1 S1" draws S1 twice (H2's root).
- ask-idle-q2: an idle "transistor Q2 P2" beside "transistor Q1 K1 P1" is told "like: transistor Q2 K1 P1" -- the
  relay and pin Q1 has; copied, Q2 still switches nothing. 36965b4 adds a contrary line for P2 ("the relay is driven
  already -- leave P2's line out").
- ask-own-line-buzzer, ask-own-line-ledk: the asked relay's line left out; 36965b4 hands back the reply's own
  transistor line, 22b1c03 "transistor Q1 BZ1 P1" / "transistor Q1 D1 P1". The line is relay K1 "12 V coil".
- ask-two-leds-dup, ask-led-spare-dup: "led D1 P2" names the existing D1 (the line is led D2 P2).
- ask-two-relays-line: the second relay's line is never given.
- ask-ldr-line: an LDR/pot/thermistor pin is never given its sensor line.
- ask-switch-dup: "switch S1 P2" when S1 is on P1 already.
- ask-base-p1, ask-nothing-pin: the transistor's line handed back is put on P1, the button's input pin, when the
  transistor is on (or must go on) P2 -- the exPin is the first pin, not the transistor's own or a free one
  (line 38139; "Q1 needs something driving its base: add pin P1 ..." is the same).
- ask-led-k1: the guide's "transistor Q1 K1 P1" copied into a button-and-LED reply is told "transistor Q1 D1 P1":
  copied, the LED's transistor sits on the button's pin.
- ask-base-r: a base resistor the model sized ("resistor R1 \"1 kohm\" Q1") is told "resistor R1 ... K1"; copied,
  Lantern never uses a resistor in series with a relay, and the same message comes back.

What 36965b4 mends, and keeps
-----------------------------
- Keeps all 20 cases afea882 put right in this set (16 drawings, 4 lines handed back: the 35B's two motor replies from Adam's laptop and set B, the guide's
  K1 for a fan, lamp, solenoid or buzzer, a load named only on the transistor's line) and all 121 right replies
  outside the T shape.
- Mends 13 more that 22b1c03 and afea882 questioned: a bare "transistor Q1" or "transistor Q1 P1" with the one load
  on its pin or none (mend-m04, mend-r03/r04/r06, mend-d02), an LED's transistor naming the guide's K1 (mend-d01), a
  push button driving a bare transistor (mend-p01), the board's name for the pin on the transistor's line with two or
  more pins (pin-01..05, pin-09).
- The bench replies (bench-*) come out as they did on all three versions.

Files
-----
cases.js           the 210 cases, each with its question, reply, what it should be, harm and why
lib.js             builds a case on a version (jsdom, through liftstation_review1_1230/load.js)
make_before.js     writes before_22b1c03.json from 22b1c03 (the "keep" and "same" baseline)
before_22b1c03.json
replay.js [file]   AGREE / DISAGREE per case, on src/lantern.inner.html or the file named
run_36965b4.txt    replay.js on 36965b4
prompts.js a b c   every bench prompt on each version, and whether they are the same
